{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXt3glg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhBSOOE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 31, "title": "Add bounded current-object UserDataNode round-trip support", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 default plugins support current-material/model references, but **ordinary `UserDataNode` instances are not supported**. In Three.js r186, `UserDataNode(property, inputType, userData = null)` can read the current rendered object's `userData` dynamically, and native GLTFExporter/GLTFLoader transport object `userData` through glTF node `extras`.

A small subset appears useful and implementable without a new TSL schema or custom resource system. **However, round-tripping the graph alone is insufficient**: GLTFLoader can produce a Group for a multi-primitive mesh and place node-level `extras` on the Group, while rendering child meshes whose `userData` may not have the same values. Do not silently redirect a missing value or claim support for such layouts.

## Expected outcome

1. Audit the installed Three.js r186 (recheck current stable during implementation):
   - `UserDataNode`, `ReferenceNode`, native reference/update behavior, constructor and runtime state, `serialize()/deserialize()` and `getSerializeChildren()`.
   - Native GLTFExporter handling of `Object3D.userData` / `nodes[*].extras`, GLTFLoader placement of extras on scene nodes vs child primitive Mesh objects, material sharing, primitive cloning, and actual plugin hooks (`writeMaterialAsync()`, `writeMesh()`, `afterParse()`, `afterRoot()`).
   - Validate source-to-imported **render-object** association, not merely JSON equality. Existing GLTF exporter/loader plugins should be extended; do not presume a Three.js core change is required.
2. Implement paired **data-only** default exporter/loader adapters for **ordinary, current-object `UserDataNode` instances** with `userData === null` and no explicit foreign `object` binding:
   - Initial target: a safe **single-level scalar `float` property** with a validated identifier and a finite numeric value present on **every rendered mesh that uses the material**. The exact property/type/side-effect allowlist must be recorded. Add `int`/`uint` or other types only if native updates, glTF extras, and repeated round trips are proven faithful; otherwise defer.
   - Export only the node's validated selector/type and necessary native state. Let ordinary glTF `extras` transport the per-object value; **do not freeze the value into the TSL graph** or add a duplicate property map to the extension. Construct real Three.js `UserDataNode` objects on import, preserving dynamic `state.object.userData` reads, sharing, and entrypoints.
   - Support ordinary single-primitive Mesh contexts whose `extras` demonstrably land on the exact Mesh used by native TSL. Support multiple meshes sharing a material when each has its own valid value. Reject unsupported exporter layouts **before emitting apparently valid graphs**, and atomically fall back on unsupported/malformed imports.
3. Proactively audit and explicitly **defer** unsafe cases rather than hiding semantic loss:
   - Multi-primitive/Group expansion, geometry/material groups and primitive clones that do not retain the value on each actual rendering Mesh; glTF scenes with missing or inconsistent `extras`; and a graph used by an object without the declared property/type.
   - Explicit/external `userData` bindings; inherited/nested property paths, unsafe/reserved names, accessors, callbacks, functions, arrays, buffers, textures, object references, `Color`/Vector values unless native glTF transport fidelity is verified.
   - `ReferenceNode` generally, independent renderer/material/object references, scene-level state, nondefault uniform-group/scheduling behavior, app-installed callbacks, and unknown native state/child links.
   - Where an exclusion could become safe with a paired geometry/node adapter or consumer-owned binding registry, document the precise binding/ownership contract required. Never rebind a foreign reference silently.
4. Reuse native Three.js property reads, NodeFrame update behavior, and existing plugin serialization/validation. Maintain the Draft v2.0 all-or-nothing fallback: unsupported or malformed node definitions (including unreachable definitions), wrong objects/extras, unknown fields/links, dangling references, cycles, or unresolvable selectors must **retain the complete ordinary glTF material including other supported extensions**; no partial graph installation.
5. Preserve the extension schema, materialType, ordinary glTF property coexistence, shared TSL singleton identity, and the absence of Draft v1.0 handling. Do not embed JavaScript, GLSL, WGSL or callbacks in glTF. No new generic property-binding framework or unrelated cleanup.

## Context and reproduction

- [Draft v2.0](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Coverage matrix: reference families and deferrals](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Current-material/model reference audit (#21)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/reference-node-support.md)
- [Existing exporter plugin (`writeMaterialAsync` / `writeMesh`)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/THREEMaterialsTSLExporterPlugin.ts)
- [Existing loader plugin (`afterRoot`)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/THREEMaterialsTSLLoaderPlugin.ts)
- [Integration tests](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [r186 UserDataNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/UserDataNode.js)
- [r186 ReferenceNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/ReferenceNode.js)
- [r186 GLTFExporter](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/examples/jsm/exporters/GLTFExporter.js)
- [r186 GLTFLoader](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js)

Representative supported goal: a single-primitive Mesh with `mesh.userData.tint = 0.5` and a mesh NodeMaterial whose `colorNode` (or another valid entrypoint) uses `userData('tint', 'float')`. After a real glTF round trip, changing the imported Mesh's `userData.tint` must update the native node when Three.js performs its normal object update.

Counterexample requiring explicit rejection or a separately proven adapter: one glTF node whose mesh expands to multiple primitive Mesh children, with node `extras.tint` attached only to their parent Group.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Audit Three.js's actual node/update and glTF extras/primitive transport paths. Document **exact** supported object/material/primitive shapes, property/type domains, and deferrals with reasons.
- [ ] Implement the minimal paired default `UserDataNode` serializer/resolver and necessary **existing-plugin** source/target render-object validation. Do not create a new extension schema, transfer an object reference, or substitute a constant.
- [ ] Add real GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader tests (JSON glTF and GLB where appropriate): supported single-primitive meshes, multiple meshes sharing one material with different userData values, node identity/sharing and entrypoints, ordinary material properties and other material extensions. Validate the **actual imported mesh.userData**, not just the scene root or Group.
- [ ] Exercise native Three.js reference updates before and after import and mutations to mesh.userData, including per-object isolation and relevant GLSL/WGSL shader-flow equivalence. Clearly separate shader generation/NodeFrame checks from browser/GPU rendering.
- [ ] Add negative exporter/import tests for missing/wrong-type/nonfinite extras, unsafe selectors, nested/external bindings, callbacks/unsupported groups, multi-primitive Group ownership, bad link shapes, unknown fields, cycles and invalid unreachable nodes. Verify **complete ordinary material fallback** and no partially applied slots.
- [ ] Update the coverage matrix, affected loader/exporter READMEs and a focused source/validation audit with the exact subset and deferral paths. Keep the Draft v2.0 README specification unchanged.
- [ ] Run and report the actual full demo integration suite, loader/exporter builds, demo typecheck/build, and `git diff --check`. Record passes, failures, warnings and skipped/unperformed validation accurately.

## Optional validation

Browser WebGL/WebGPU visual checks for live per-mesh userData changes. If not run, state clearly that native Node-side update/shader checks do not establish GPU compilation or rendered pixels.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **No npm publication or version bump as part of this issue.** The maintainer handles `npm publish` manually as a separate release step.
